thread:
samir: heads-up — acme-prod reporting p99 spikes on /v1/generate around 10:12 PDT. only on short prompts (<10 tokens). customer says sudden regressions after last config change. request ids: r-8f3c, r-8f3d, r-8f40

jess: which cluster/region? any error codes?

samir: us-west-2, hosted pool gp3-a. no 5xxs, just high tail latency. p95 jumped 230ms -> 580ms, p99 from 490ms -> 1.5s for that tenant. other tenants unaffected.

maya: pulled traces for r-8f3c, looks like early queueing inside continuous-batcher. lots of tiny requests getting coalesced and then one or two late arrivals are pushing batch creation.

leo: that sounds like hold-window vs batch-size tradeoff. did we rollout the longer grace window yesterday?

samir: yes — grace_ms bumped 10 -> 18 in the canary applied to gp3-a at 09:45. change was to reduce CPU overhead for medium prompts.

katie: quick repro on dev: send 1000 short requests (2–6 tokens) at 120rps to a single shard, see p99 ~1.4s. repro steps:
```
ab -n 1000 -c 40 -p tiny_payload.json https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate
# tiny_payload.json has prompt of 3 tokens
```

maya: logs from runtime:
```
[2026-03-16T10:12:31Z] batch_create shard=gp3-a batch_id=342 size=6 hold_ms=18 wait_ms=180 pending=[r-8f3c,r-8f3d,...]
[2026-03-16T10:12:31Z] late_arrival r-8f40 added_to_batch batch_id=342 latency_delta=980ms
[2026-03-16T10:12:31Z] dispatch batch_id=342 runtime_exec_ms=45
```

jess: so late arrivals are delaying the whole batch. default behavior is to wait up to hold_ms for coalescing. increasing hold_ms reduces CPU churn but increases tail if traffic is bursty/sparse.

leo: mitigation options: 1) lower grace_ms back to 10 2) enable tiny-request fast-path (greedy dispatch for <=4 tokens) 3) per-tenant override (acme-prod only) 4) fallback to single-request sync for short prompts.

samir: can we do per-tenant override quickly? acme is paying enterprise SLA.

katie: we have feature flag rollout for per-tenant batching policies. can flip for acme in console now. I can toggle to "aggressive_dispatch" which sets hold_ms=6 for that tenant.

maya: empirical note: aggressive_dispatch dropped p99 from 1.5s -> 260ms in dev repro. increased CPU by ~8% but within pool headroom.

ops-bot: deploy-job #deploy-457 queued by katie — staging tests pass.

samir: katie please flip and watch acme metrics; if green we'll roll to other affected customers. also open a ticket to revert cluster-wide grace_ms change and add canary checks for tiny-prompt p99 regressions.

katie: done — flipped per-tenant policy for acme-prod at 10:35. monitoring dashboard: p99 back to 270ms within 4m.

jess: followups: 1) revert cluster-wide grace_ms bump and re-evaluate canary gate 2) add synthetic tiny-prompt probes in the canary suite (p95/p99 targets) 3) doc runbook for batching tradeoffs + recommended per-tenant policies 4) notify account team / CS with RCA and mitigation notes.

samir: adding to backlog: BUG-1278 revert grace_ms change + add canary metric. assigning to eng-runtime.

maya: small note for postmortem — consider adding adaptive hold: dynamically reduce hold_ms when avg tokens/request < X or when short-request share > Y. would reduce manual tuning.

katie: agreement. I'll create a short RFC and slot it for next week.

samir: thanks all. acme confirmed restored. leaving this thread open for postmortem updates.
